newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch down in slow dealing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch down in slow dealing.

text.p: Mexican stocks edged down at the open on Monday due to what traders said was a retreat from Friday's record close amid a slow market awaiting fresh political and economic news.
"The market's dead, most heavyweights have yet to open. They closed up on Friday for month-end valuation purposes, so they will ease down a little," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 1.92 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.04 percent, at 4,479.19.
Trading volume was thin at just 523,000 shares.
"Nothing's happening," a floor trader said. "Telmex ADRs are down, so I would imagine it will open down here and weigh down the market a little."
"I expect the market to be on hold for most of this week, with the FOMC meeting, U.S. Independence Day and domestic mid-term elections," the desk trader added.
The Federal Open Market Committee will meet on Wednesday to review interest rates, and U.S. financial markets will close on Friday for the Independence Day holiday.
Mexico will hold mid-term elections on Sunday, July 6.

Most heavily traded were financial stock Bancomer, down 5 centavos to 3.87 pesos, which weighed most on the market. Paper company Kimberly Clark de Mxico was another active stock, up 20 centavos to 31.10 pesos. Kimberly-Clark Corp has a minority stake in the Mexican company.
ADRs listed by market heavyweight Telfonos de Mxico (Telmex) were off 1/2 to 47-5/8. The telecom's L shares had, unusually, not opened in early trade.
